applies_why: The judge assigns a rating (UNDERDETERMINED) for a verse dispute, so the rule on what that rating may rest on applies.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase 'thy father' is immediately qualified by the child's reference to 'my Father's business.'
rule_words: A judge may not rest STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED on one verse failing to state a link or its contrary.
room: 'failing to state a link or its contrary': one reading is that the judge must not rest a verdict on a verse's silence; the other is that any one-verse verdict is barred. I weighed the narrow reading (silence) against the broad reading (any single-verse basis).
why: The judge does not rest on the verse's silence but on its positive content ('thy father' being qualified within the verse itself) plus the defender's written answers, so the verdict is not built on a verse merely failing to state a link or its contrary.
